transcribedBy: opus-agent gap hunt civ-start + blind re-read

fills.name: Northern Migration
fills.note: Starting Villager Capacity: the Villager counter reads 6/10 at game time 00:02, before any Longhouse exists. Each Longhouse adds +10. The Overview reads 'The Villager Capacity is increased by +10 for each Longhouse constructed.' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00012.jpg). The Longhouse tooltip reads 'Increases your Villager capacity by +10 and your maximum Population by +25.' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00174.jpg). The HUD then goes 6/10 -> 10/20 -> 16/30 (nd74LibluQ0 1:38, 5:25, 7:10). The highest capacity seen in any recording is 200 (e.g. nd74LibluQ0 41:40, 72/200). That is not proven to be a hard maximum.
fills.tieReason: There is no tooltip in this frame, but the HUD counter at the top left of the villager panel reads 6/10 at 00:02, at game start with only the Town Center built. The OCR series for the same slot in ehO1BOe7wG8 shows what the counter is. The first number rises by 1 about every 22 s (6/10 at t140, 7/10 at t162, 8/10 at t186), which is the Northern Migration auto-recruit interval. The second number goes up in steps of +10 as Longhouses are built (9/20 at t212, then 20/30 and 20/40). It moves separately from the population counter, which reads 7/10, then 13/35 and 22/85. So the counter is current villagers over Villager Capacity, and capacity before any Longhouse is 10. This matches the narration in nd74LibluQ0 and uNw-K34ZDPs ('limited to 10 villagers').

fills.name: Northern Migration (detail)
fills.note: A second recording (Drongo vs AI) shows the same base Villager Capacity of 10 at game time 00:07. The capacity rises by +10 per Longhouse; Longhouse cost is 150 wood, 30s.
fills.tieReason: The SAGAS tooltip at 00:07 belongs to the 0/7 icon next to this counter. The villager-capacity counter beside it reads 6/10, with 6 villagers and no Longhouse built. In the same video (uNw-K34ZDPs) the slot reads 6/10, 7/10, 8/10, then 8/20, 9/20 and later 20/30, 20/40. Each +10 step comes when a Longhouse is built, and the counter differs from population (11/35, 33/110). That makes it the Northern Migration Villager Capacity, and its value at game start is 10. The narrator in this video agrees: 'we are currently limited to 10 villagers'.

fills.name: Northern Migration (detail)
fills.value: Villagers are automatically recruited from the Town Center at no cost whenever there is spare Villager Capacity. Start: 6 Villagers, capacity 10. Each Longhouse adds +10 Villager Capacity and +25 max population. The HUD warns 'Villager capacity almost reached build more Longhouses' and then 'Villager capacity reached build more Longhouses'. Falkr's Village Saga reduces Villager recruitment time by 2 seconds.
fills.quote: NORTHERN MIGRATION Information Villagers are automatically recruited at no cost as long as there is spare Villager Capacity. Villager Capacity is increased by constructing more Longhouses.
fills.note: Tooltip on the Town Center (game 00:10, HUD 6/10). The Saga text 'Villager recruitment speed reduced by 2 seconds and Longhouse attachment cost reduced by 20%.' is from the Overview (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00012.jpg). The capacity warning toast is in qARfRxyhRhA/s_00298.jpg. Proof that recruitment is free: in ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00174.jpg (game 00:35) food is still 0 while the Villager counter has risen to 7/10.

fills.name: Imperial population
fills.value: Both Age IV landmarks increase population and maximum population by +10, so max population goes from 200 to 210. Kongens Dør Cathedral (Age IV Economic Landmark) acts as a Monastery and has a unique technology (Folkekirken) that adds another +10, for 220. Rikets Nyckel Castle (Age IV Defensive Landmark) gives +10 only (210).
fills.quote: Kongens Dør Cathedral Age IV - Economic Landmark 2400 1200 4m 10s Acts as a Monastery. Increases population and maximum population by +10. Has a slowly expanding area that gathers a tithe of 10 Gold for each Longhouse every 30 seconds. Has a unique technology that further increases maximum population. | Rikets Nyckel Castle Age IV - Defensive Landmark 2400 1200 4m 10s Acts as a Keep that fires volleys of arrows. Increases population and maximum population by +10. Reduces the cost of all unit tier technologies by 50%. Recruits 10 Skåne Crossbowmen upon construction completion.
fills.note: HUD shows 128/200 on this frame (game 22:41). The same game reads 128/220 next to 'Folkekirken completed' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_01532.jpg, game 23:13). After Rikets Nyckel Castle the HUD reads 31/210 (BV182n46EEDi_p2/s_00667.jpg, game 08:26).

fills.name: Late-game roster shift
fills.value: In Castle Age (III) the Vikings get two cheaper, weaker variants of standard units. The Stable gets the Jylland Knight (Heavy Melee Cavalry, 120 food 90 gold, 'Lower cost but with reduced damage and health', grants 10 Gold on death). The Archery Range gets Skåne Crossbowmen (Light Ranged Infantry, 75 food 30 gold, 'Lower cost but with reduced damage and health'). Both read 'Requirements: Castle Age (III)'.
fills.quote: JYLLAND KNIGHT Heavy Melee Cavalry 120 90 Unique to Vikings Expensive cavalry with high damage and melee armor. Effective against melee units. Lower cost but with reduced damage and health. + Heavy armor + Strong in melee combat + Grants 10 Gold on death - Countered by Spearmen and Crossbowmen Requirements: Castle Age (III)
fills.note: Skåne tooltip is in the frame next door, uNw-K34ZDPs/s_01132.jpg (18:52): 'SKÅNE CROSSBOWMEN Light Ranged Infantry 75 30 Unique to Vikings High damage ranged unit best against heavy targets. Lower cost but with reduced damage and health. + Anti-heavy specialist - Low health - Countered by Horsemen Requirements: Castle Age (III)'. Valdemar Castle (Age III) makes Jylland Knights grant 20 more Gold on death (uNw-K34ZDPs/s_01010.jpg). Whether these replace the regular Knight and Crossbowman is not stated on screen.

fills.name: Starting conditions
fills.value: Start: 6 Villagers, 1 Scout and 1 Highland Cattle, with 200 food, 200 wood, 100 gold and 0 stone. Population reads 7/10 (the cattle does not count toward population). Highland Cattle counter reads 1/9: cattle capacity starts at 9 and rises by 4 with every Highland Landmark.
fills.note: I counted the units in a zoomed crop: 6 villagers with sleep (Z) marks, 1 Highland Cattle with a Z mark, 1 mounted scout without one. The idle counter '7' is 6 villagers plus the cattle. Resources are read before Corvinus used cheats at 00:09. Corroborated by OCna8RhsP9E/s_00016.jpg (200/200/100/0, 1/9, 7/10). The Overview reads 'They begin with a capacity of 9, and that increases by 4 with every Highland Landmark built.' and gives 'Food at a rate of 30 per minute' (BV1Bmnx6ZEBh_p2/s_01200.jpg). Beasty's c_oaynL66jY lobby used non-standard resources (50000/50050/25000/10000), so ignore it for this.

fills.name: Starting conditions
fills.value: Start: 6 Villagers and 1 Scout, with 0 food, 200 wood, 100 gold and 0 stone. Villager Capacity reads 6/10, population 7/10, Sagas 0/7. Villagers are then auto-recruited for free (Northern Migration).
fills.note: Not in the gap list; vikings.json has a 'Starting conditions' bonus saying 'Not stated anywhere'. Same HUD at game 00:01 (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00141.jpg). A second recording shows 0/200/100/0 at 00:07 (uNw-K34ZDPs/s_00048.jpg). Food is still 0 at 00:35 with 7/10 villagers (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00174.jpg). The scout is the horseman left of the Town Center; 6 villagers plus the scout make 7/10 population.
